name: Thenameda Form Payments with SagePay for WPForms
author: Imtiyaj

sections.description:
Thenameda Form Payments with SagePay for WPForms lets you accept SagePay (Opayo) payments on any WPForms form. Configure credentials and field mapping per form in the WPForms form builder. When a visitor submits the form they are redirected to the Opayo hosted payment page to pay securely. After payment, they return to your site and the transaction is stored in your dashboard.

Works with WPForms Lite and WPForms Pro.

Features

  • Per-form SagePay settings inside the WPForms form builder (Settings » SagePay).
  • SagePay / Opayo Form integration with AES-128-CBC encrypted crypt payload.
  • Sandbox (test) and Live modes with separate vendor credentials.
  • Transaction types: Payment, Deferred, Authenticate.
  • Optional 3D Secure request.
  • Map amount, quantity, email, and billing/shipping address fields.
  • Supports WPForms Name and Address fields (components read automatically).
  • Optional “shipping same as billing”.
  • Configurable success and failure return URLs.
  • [sagepay-details] shortcode for payment result display.
  • Transaction listing with status badges, detail view, and CSV export.
  • Improved redirect interstitial and payment toast notifications.

External Services

This plugin connects to the Opayo (SagePay) payment service operated by Elavon to process card payments via the hosted Form protocol.

What data is sent and when

Data is sent only when SagePay is enabled for a form and a visitor is redirected to pay:

  1. Form submission — The plugin encrypts payment amount, currency, description, customer email/name, billing and delivery address fields, return URLs, and vendor email, then POSTs the encrypted Crypt value with Vendor name and transaction type to Opayo (sandbox.opayo.eu.elavon.com or live.opayo.eu.elavon.com).
  2. Return from Opayo — Opayo redirects the buyer back with an encrypted crypt response that the plugin decrypts to record transaction status.

Card details are entered on Opayo’s hosted page and never touch your WordPress site.

Opayo / Elavon policies

  • Privacy Policy: https://www.elavon.com/privacy-policy.html
  • Opayo overview: https://www.elavon.co.uk/payment-platforms/opayo.html
sections.installation:
1. Make sure WPForms Lite or WPForms is installed and active.
  2. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install it from the Plugins screen.
  3. Activate the plugin through the “Plugins” menu in WordPress.
  4. Edit a form, open Settings » SagePay, enable SagePay, enter your Opayo credentials, and map billing fields.
  5. Save the form and place it on a page.
sections.faq:
Where do I get SagePay / Opayo credentials?

Log in to MySagePay / Opayo and open your Form integration settings to copy the Vendor Name and Encryption Password for Sandbox and Live.

How is the payment amount determined?

Select an “Amount field” in the SagePay settings, or leave it on the default to use the WPForms payment total. An optional quantity field multiplies the amount. A fixed amount can be used as a fallback.

Which country format is required?

SagePay expects ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes (for example GB, IE, US). State is required only for US addresses.

Where can I see payments?

Under SagePay Transactions in the WordPress admin menu. Optionally add [sagepay-details] on your success page.
